# Matching models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

1 matching models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both.

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 768x1024: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory). – = not measured.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## RoMa v2

RoMa v2 (2025): dense matching between two photos of one scene from any viewpoints: where each pixel of the first image is in the second, and how sure the model is that it is visible there. Built on Meta's DINOv3. MIT code; the DINOv3 parts of the code and weights are under the DINOv3 licence.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `romav2` | synthetic (768x1024) | original (fp32)<br>original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 1412<br>741<br>546<br>406<br>576<br>353 | 11159 / 11606<br>9881 / 10124<br>1989 / 2596<br>1909 / 2580<br>3150 / 3386<br>5702 (engine) |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Original code: <https://github.com/Parskatt/romav2> at `95c9968145c8`
- Code licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License (permissive); files: `LICENSE`, `LICENSE.md`
- Weights licence: MIT AND LicenseRef-DINOv3-License
- Licence evidence: <https://github.com/Parskatt/romav2/blob/95c9968145c8906b7b59383258e9f73b02853d89/README.md#license>
- Training data: Upstream README: a mix of wide-baseline matching datasets following UFM and MapAnything (MegaDepth and others; see the paper); none has a dataset entry here yet. The frozen DINOv3 descriptor was pretrained on LVD-1689M (not released).
- Licence note: The checkpoint includes the DINOv3 ViT-L/16 weights, and net/dinov3.py and net/vit/ come from DINOv3: the DINOv3 License (Meta: attribution and conditions apply) covers those parts; read it before commercial use.
- Options: `coarse_size` = 800 (>= 16), `fine_size` = 1280 (>= 0)
- Kernel libraries: `romav2`
- Variants: `romav2`
- Outputs: warp, certainty
- Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `romav2` 3000x4000 (2.9 GiB peak allocated, 4.7 reserved)
- `romav2` 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 254 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 185 s (ONNX + engine).
- `romav2` original (fp32) 768x1024: upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)
- `romav2` original 768x1024: the authors' mixed-precision option (bfloat16); upstream RoMaV2.match; local correlation: upstream's plain-torch path (no fused-local-corr)
- `romav2` load / first call: original 5.45 s / 2.091 s, portable 0.85 s / 0.913 s, kernels 1.5 s / 0.812 s
- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

### Measured

5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling), OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

| variant | dataset | original fp32 | original fp16 | portable | kernels | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `romav2` | MegaDepth-1500, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees |  | 63.2 / 77.1 / 86.7 | 63.0 / 76.9 / 86.5 | 62.9 / 76.9 / 86.4 |  |
| `romav2` | MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees | 64.6 / 78.0 / 87.1 | 64.7 / 78.2 / 87.3 | 64.7 / 78.3 / 87.3 | 64.4 / 77.9 / 86.9 |  |

Measured on portable: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 011e320c, 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-12; kernels: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130, fastforks 011e320c, 2026-11-12.

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 1.6e-05 vs the original. GPU, bfloat16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0086 and p99 <= 0.032 (absolute error of the output `warp`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `romav2` | 0.00573 / 0.02077 | RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130 | `romav2@1c8e19405d40:sm_120` |

### Limitations

- The precision matrices of the warp (upstream `precision_AB`) and upstream's sampling / keypoint helpers are not returned; tools/eval_matching.py has the MegaDepth-1500 sampling.
- Both images are resized to squares (upstream's behaviour), whatever their aspect ratio.
